status: DRAFT - not frozen; discovery disabled until every pre-freeze gate is closed; Phase 1 tool building is allowed and never counts as Stage A evidence. PROTOCOL.md is the readable version; if they disagree before freezing, PROTOCOL.md wins.
question: Can we establish, independently of LARQL, whether a LARQL-encoded model faithfully reconstructs its upstream checkpoint: empirically (A), with proven bounds for selected operations (B), and with at least one machine-checked bound (C)?

baseline.larql_sha: a clean LARQL commit (no modified or untracked files), pinned at freeze; the audit was done at ff364ba6, whose tree was dirty
baseline.subject: Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B, official BF16 checkpoint (not a community GGUF), HF commit c1899de289a04d12100db370d81485cdf75e47ca; never a floating main
baseline.encoding: Q8_0 only, from vindex3 represent --encoding Q8_0 with the default role policy; NVFP4 and Q4_K are later subjects
baseline.upstream: every file of that commit pinned by SHA-256 (upstream_pin); the encoded container's SHA-256 is recorded too
baseline.backend: CPU: vindex3 exec --backend production-q8 --representation-source stored --logit-dump; Metal out of scope
baseline.environment: LARQL_CPU_MAX_FORMAT=bf16; LARQL_KQUANT_EXEC, LARQL_CPU_ARITHMETIC and LARQL_CPU_WORKERS pinned at freeze; every other LARQL_* unset; the harness records the full LARQL_* environment and a run with an unexpected variable is invalid
baseline.execution_mode: teacher-forced, KV-cached decode, one token at a time, batch size 1 (the only mode LARQL's logit dump provides); prefill out of scope
baseline.gap: spec.verify.reconstruction and spec.verify.logit_match are declared but unsupported (crates/larql-factory/src/build/stages/verify.rs:22-32, commit d8a7d730)

upstream_pin.verified: 2026-10-30, computed locally from the download; matches HF LFS SHA-256 for LFS files and HF git blob IDs for the rest; 311 tensors, all BF16, tied embeddings, rms_norm_eps 1e-6, rope_theta 1e6, no RoPE scaling, no sliding window

trusted_base.ggml ggml-quants.c (commit pinned at fre: Q8_0 numerical semantics and the reference encoder for the T2 bound
trusted_base.gguf-py 0.18.0 gguf.quants.Q8_0: third-party cross-check of the checker's decode
trusted_base.IEEE 754-2019 binary16/binary32: f16 to f32 conversion, signed zero, subnormals, non-finite values
trusted_base.LARQL published container specification: container framing only: segment framing, index.json, tensor table, dtype labels, row orientation, Q8_0 block layout within a row, LARQL-name to HF-key map, role policy; never numerical semantics; a conflict with ggml is a core ambiguity; admissible only after a third party (neither its author nor the reference-checker agent) confirms it describes the files LARQL emits at the freeze commit
trusted_base.transformers 5.5.0 on torch 2.14.0: reference forward pass for E2 and E3
trusted_base.lockfile: frozen; changing a pinned version after freezing counts as editing a frozen file

acceptance.A0_analytic_positive_cases: the checker's decode equals hand-derived f32 bit patterns on every Q8_0 decode case: q in {127, -128, 0}; d in {+0, -0, smallest and largest f16 subnormal, smallest normal, 65504, negative, +inf, -inf, NaN}; little-endian f16, int8 sign, block and row order. Encoder-side cases (roundf ties, f16 rounding of d, amax=0, subnormal d, overflow, non-finite inputs) are required for E1 fixtures. Decode ties, min/offset scales, sub-block scales, nibble order, non-finite codes and code saturation are vacuous for Q8_0
acceptance.A1_reconstruction: checker correctness: A0 passes, the checker's decode matches gguf-py 0.18.0 bit for bit on every tensor, unquantised tensors decode exactly (T1). LARQL's own decode is not observable; the required decode is that of the stored bytes per spec, and LARQL's use of it is observed through E2. Reported: E1 per tensor, block-level distribution, count of T2 exceedances and of zero-scale blocks
acceptance.A2_logit_match: E1, E2 (same decoded weights, LARQL vs reference) and E3 (LARQL vs original checkpoint) reported separately, in teacher-forced KV-cached decode. The checker's harness records and matches token IDs, container SHA-256, backend arm, full LARQL_* environment and worker count, config, positional encoding, masking, execution mode, accumulation dtype and the quantised-tensor set; a mismatch makes the comparison invalid. Checker correctness: preconditions hold, metrics computed correctly, A4 logit rows behave. Reported: E2 against T3; E3 under T4, judged against nothing. Metrics: max |delta|, RMS delta, KL and top-1 over the same full vocabulary in the same token-ID order (size mismatch invalid). KL = D_KL(P_reference || P_candidate) in nats, from f32 logits promoted to f64 via max-subtracted log-softmax in f64; terms with p_ref = 0 contribute 0. Top-1 ties go to the lowest token ID, comparing f32 values
acceptance.A3_reproduce_self_checks: S5, IP1-IP3, codec bit-exactness and S6 reproduced from outside LARQL; any disagreement is a finding
acceptance.A4_fault_rejection: frozen fault-detection matrix: every claimed guarantee has at least one relevant corruption (must be rejected) and at least one valid control (must be accepted); the reviewer holds the hidden rows

A.falsified_if: a behaviour-changing mutation is accepted; the checker's decode differs from A0 or from gguf-py and the cause is not traced; an E2 discrepancy beyond T3 is left untraced; a tolerance or the pilot rule is changed after measurements on the subject have been seen
A.acceptance_rule: Stage A is accepted on checker correctness only; tolerance results are reported as model acceptability and never fail Stage A

tolerance_rules.T1_exact_decode: each Q8_0 element decodes to f32(q)*f32(d), compared as a bit pattern; unquantised tensors decode exactly; reason: the product is exact in f32
tolerance_rules.T2_reconstruction_bound: |x - q*d16| <= d16*(1/2 + 2^-12 + 2^-16 + 127*2^-11) + 127*2^-25, derived from ggml's reference encoder; LARQL's truncating, flush-to-zero f32->f16 (half.rs:43-60) is known to exceed it, and that is reported as a model-acceptability finding without widening the bound; empirically checked (19.2M simulated weights, no violations, worst ratio 0.9999), not proven: a universal claim needs independent review of the derivation as a Stage B result; the checker never copies LARQL's half.rs conversion into its decoder, fixtures or expected values
tolerance_rules.T3_execution_agreement: per logit |LARQL - ref32| <= max(c*|ref32 - ref64|, k*ulp32(ref64)); form fixed a priori; c and k from a preregistered pilot on another checkpoint (candidate SmolLM2-135M) or a discarded disjoint corpus, using the smallest ladder values (c in {2,4,8,16,32}, k in {4,16,64}) that pass every pilot logit, plus one step of margin; pilot data never enter results
tolerance_rules.T4_end_to_end: report_only: no acceptance threshold; reports max |delta|, RMS delta, KL and top-1 agreement per position with distributions; never affects the Stage A verdict; no post-hoc promotion of an observed value into a pass; no claim of behavioural equivalence on all prompts; a quantitative E3 requirement belongs to a later campaign

B.acceptance: a written derivation or sound tool certificate of the bound over an explicit input domain (holding for any summation order, or with a named order as a testable assumption); adversarial review finds no gap; empirical drift never exceeds the bound (sanity check only)
B.falsified_if: an input inside the domain exceeds the bound; the derivation relies on an assumption the kernel violates; the domain is narrowed after measurements have been seen

C.acceptance: Lean 4 checks the theorem with no sorry; a trust ledger lists every axiom, floating-point model assumption and implementation claim Lean does not check
C.not_claimed: that LARQL's Rust or Metal code is verified

anti_cheat: the agent cannot edit frozen files, corpora, tolerances, the mutation suite or the frozen checker (enforced by manifest); LARQL self-reports never decide a verdict; no result is reported with a stronger kind of guarantee than it has
secondary_observations_not_acceptance: how far measured error falls below the bound

scope.in: reconstruction and logit match for the one declared subject and Q8_0 encoding on one CPU backend in teacher-forced KV-cached decode; error bounds for single operations; one Lean theorem
out: head interventions outside CPU softmax decode
NVFP4, Q4_K and other encodings (later subjects)

open_decisions.B2_subject: DECIDED 2026-10-30: Qwen3-0.6B official BF16 at the pinned commit
open_decisions.B1_freeze_lock: OPEN; owner: a freeze owner outside the research agent plus a named human reviewer. Protected remote branch and pinned freeze commit; CI verifies the manifest against the protected reference; the research agent cannot alter the reference, manifest, CI workflow or required checks; nine tamper tests run as the agent role, each rejected at the outside point, evidence kept; the freeze owner owns the protected reference, branch protection and required checks; tamper test 6 includes leaving frozen files unchanged while altering the verifier or CI workflow so a corrupted manifest passes; evidence includes a legitimate pass and every rejection, with commit hashes and the deciding CI run
open_decisions.B3_container_spec: OPEN; owner: LARQL maintainer or a separate specification author, never the reference-checker agent. Covers byte layout, offsets, alignment, endianness, segment framing, index.json and tensor metadata, name-to-HF-key map, role policy (incl. tied embedding and LM head), integrity rules, versioning. Not Q8_0 arithmetic, tolerances or reference execution. A third party checks it against emitted files before it is trusted; every tensor's representation type and quantisation metadata discoverable from the container without knowing the role policy; tied embeddings stated separately as logical identity, physical storage, numerical representation and which representation the output projection executes
open_decisions.L1_clean_larql_commit: OPEN; a reproducibility gate, not evidence of correctness: no modified or untracked files; an auditor (not the reference-checker agent) re-checks the production-q8 path, the Q8_0 encoder's f32->f16 conversion, tied-embedding encoding and execution, and the pinned LARQL_* configuration at that commit (G3 evidence); the container is encoded fresh from the pinned checkpoint at that commit; ~/chris-models/qwen3-0.6b.vindex3 is excluded from acceptance evidence

pre_freeze_gates.G1_freeze_integrity: open: manifest plus outside check, shown by tamper tests including attempts by the researcher
pre_freeze_gates.G2_independence: open: roles, isolation, forbidden dependencies, hidden-fault procedure
pre_freeze_gates.G4_numerical_contract: open: one checkpoint and one encoding, what is compared, tolerance rules before measurement, no Metal
pre_freeze_gates.G7_stage_B_domain_written_down: open: Stage B's format is chosen at G7 on its own merits (Q8_0 for continuity, or another format with a stated scientific reason); the Stage A choice does not decide it

verdicts.checker_correctness: decided by the fault-detection matrix and the reviewer's independently derived results; Stage A is accepted on this
verdicts.model_acceptability: reported for each encoding as an outcome; an encoding over tolerance is a correct finding, not a Stage A failure

roles.reference_checker_agent: builds from independent specs; has no access to LARQL source or hidden cases
roles.larql_implementation_agent: integrates accepted checks; no access to the reference checker's internals, the criteria or hidden cases
roles.independent_reviewer: generates hidden faults, verifies provenance, independently derives selected expected results; does not take either agent's self-reports as evidence

ambiguity_policy: spec ambiguities are logged in AMBIGUITIES.md (passage, readings, chosen reading, reason, scope core/optional) and never settled by inspecting LARQL; no LARQL-generated fixtures; shared dependencies only if declared in the trusted base; LARQL's published container spec is admissible for framing only

freeze_decision.reviewer_given: the requirements, the readiness audit and repo read access
freeze_decision.reviewer_not_given: the drafting rationale or preferred outcome
freeze_decision.stage_A_implementation: Stage A runs not before READY TO FREEZE; tools may be built beforehand under phase_1

phase_1.phases: 1 build the verification system now; 2 freeze after READY TO FREEZE; 3 run Stage A
phase_1.allowed: B1 freeze mechanism and tamper tests (freeze owner); B3 container spec from LARQL's implementation (spec author, may read LARQL) and its third-party check; L1 clean worktree, pinned commit, fresh Q8_0 encoding, production-q8 audit (may read LARQL); independent checker: Q8_0 decoder from ggml, container reader from the admitted B3 spec, reference harness (no LARQL source, fixtures, tests or docs besides B3); A0 fixtures and hidden fault rows (reviewer, kept from the checker agent)
phase_1.rules: nothing counts toward Stage A, and every Stage A result is reproduced after the freeze by the frozen checker; checker isolation is enforced, not instructed, and recorded from its first commit, and code produced after any breach is discarded; the checker is not run on LARQL's Qwen3 container or logit dumps before the freeze; the T3 pilot is not run in Phase 1; the freeze review is not weakened and its snapshot includes the Phase 1 evidence records
